newsitem.title: UK: France's Superphenix reactor to shut for six month.
newsitem.headline: France's Superphenix reactor to shut for six month.

text.p: France's prototype Superphenix fast-breeder nuclear reactor is to shut down next week for six months ahead of a conversion to burn plutonium, the nuclear industry news agency NucNet said on Friday.
Superphenix operator NERSA said on Friday the 1,200 megawatt plant would be shut in preparation for a new dual role as a plutonium burner as well as a breeder.
NERSA said that during the outage, fuel assemblies would be moved inside the core, a move aimed at reducing the fast breeder character of the reactor.
The 60 billion franc Superphenix reactor, which has recently been operating at 90 percent of capacity, has had a troubled history.

Since it was commissioned 20 years ago it has operated for only a dozen months and faced pressure from environmental groups who want the plant, near the southeastern alpine city of Grenoble, to be closed permanently.
